content: 1. Follow the manufacturer's color-coding for the sequence of norethindrone acetate/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous fumarate administration. Exercise caution and monitor blood pressure during use. Do not administer this combination to premenarchal individuals, as it is not recommended. 2. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of fezolinetant by altering hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors increases fezolinetant's AUC and peak plasma concentration. 3. Ethinyl estradiol, when co-administered with ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir, can lead to significant ALT elevations (>5x ULN, including some >20x ULN). Discontinue ethinyl estradiol-containing medications before initiating hepatitis C combination therapy and restart them approximately two weeks after completing the regimen. 4. Co-administration of tranexamic acid and ethinyl estradiol increases the risk of thrombosis due to pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Acitretin reduces the efficacy of norethindrone acetate through an unknown mechanism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; use a nonhormonal contraceptive method instead. 7. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid concurrent use of anastrozole with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 8. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may lose efficacy; use nonhormonal contraceptive methods during treatment. 9. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; use a nonhormonal contraceptive method instead. 10. Ferrous fumarate reduces the absorption of baloxavir marboxil in the gastrointestinal tract due to cation binding. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Atazanavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; use a nonhormonal contraceptive method instead. 12. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding may occur. Use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment. 13. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; use a nonhormonal contraceptive method instead. 14. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable; use alternative contraception. 15. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may lose efficacy. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least four months after the last dose. 16. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; use a nonhormonal contraceptive method instead. 17. Calaspargase pegol may indirectly interact with oral contraceptives, reducing their efficacy. Use a non-oral contraceptive method for females of childbearing potential. 18. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; use a nonhormonal contraceptive method instead. 19. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 20. Ferrous fumarate reduces the absorption of demeclocycline in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 21. Dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; use a nonhormonal contraceptive method instead. 22. Ferrous fumarate reduces the absorption of doxycycline in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; use a nonhormonal contraceptive method instead. 24. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of elagolix through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for one week after discontinuation. 25. Ferrous fumarate reduces the absorption of eltrombopag in the gastrointestinal tract. Separate administration by at least four hours. 26. Elvitegravir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Consider alternative nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 27. Enasidenib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting specific transporters. Avoid co-administration or adjust the substrate dosage as needed. 28. Encorafenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may lose efficacy. Use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment. 29. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of enoxaparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 30. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable; use alternative contraception. 31. Elicarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use additional or alternative nonhormonal birth control. 32. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of exemestane through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid concurrent use with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 34. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of fedratinib by inhibiting specific enzymes. Avoid co-administration or adjust the substrate dosage as needed. 35. Ferrous fumarate reduces the absorption of fleroxacin in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 36. Fosamprenavir may alter hormone levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Use alternative nonhormonal contraception. 37. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable; use alternative contraception. 38. Ferrous fumarate reduces the absorption of gemifloxacin in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 39. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; use a nonhormonal contraceptive method instead. 40. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of heparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 41. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 42. Indinavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; use a nonhormonal contraceptive method instead. 43. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or monitor for therapeutic loss if unavoidable. 44. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Leniolisib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting specific transporters. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug.
